# Environment variables an external build tool may inherit from the caller.
#
# The Rust build scripts embed this file at compile time and
# build_environ.py reads it from the staged driver directory, so the Rust
# steps and the Python drivers hand their tools the same environment. One
# variable name per line; a line starting with # is a comment.
#
# Nothing listed here changes what a tool produces. Every
# output-affecting value (compilers, flags, the SDK) is set explicitly by
# the step that runs the tool and is part of that step's hashed arguments.
# That is also why the retained values are never hashed: PATH differs
# between shells on one machine, and hashing it would rebuild CPython on
# every shell change.
#
# Dropped by omission: CPATH and C_INCLUDE_PATH (header injection into
# the compiler), CFLAGS, CXXFLAGS, CPPFLAGS, LDFLAGS, and LIBS (CMake,
# OpenSSL's Configure, and autoconf seed their flags from them),
# LIBRARY_PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH, PKG_CONFIG_PATH, every CMAKE_*
# variable (toolchain file, compiler launcher, prefix and module paths),
# MAKEFLAGS, PERL5OPT and PERL5LIB (code injection into Configure), and
# every PYTHON* variable. LC_ALL is set to C on top of this list.
#
# The CI guard's variables are not listed: the guard runs inside the build
# runner and the Python drivers, which receive the full environment, never
# inside a tool.
#
# The list is one list on every host. A name a host does not define is
# simply absent from the parent environment and never reaches a tool, so a
# per-host list would buy nothing and would let the Rust and Python readers
# drift apart.

# Tool discovery: where cmake, ninja, make, perl, and python are found.
PATH
# Per-user state of host tools: pip's configuration, xcrun's caches.
HOME
# Scratch space; some hosts have no writable default location.
TMPDIR
# macOS: the Xcode or command-line-tools installation that cc resolves to.
DEVELOPER_DIR

# Windows OS plumbing. These are not tool configuration: they are how the
# platform itself works, and a process without them cannot load a DLL, run
# a batch file, or open a temporary file. INCLUDE, LIB, LIBPATH and the
# CL/_CL_ pair are deliberately still absent, for the same reason CPATH and
# CFLAGS are: they inject headers, libraries, and compiler options. The one
# builder that needs the MSVC environment (OpenSSL's nmake build) discovers
# the installation itself and exports those variables from inside the step,
# where the toolchain version joins the step's hashed arguments.
#
# The loader's own search root; without it every DLL load fails.
SystemRoot
# The same directory under its older name, which some tools still read.
windir
# The volume SystemRoot lives on, used to compose absolute paths.
SystemDrive
# cmd.exe's own path. Spawning a .bat or .cmd wrapper goes through it.
ComSpec
# Which extensions name a program, for bare-name resolution.
PATHEXT
# Scratch space. Windows has no /tmp, so a tool with neither is stuck.
TEMP
# The same scratch space under the name the older CRT reads.
TMP
# The home directory. Windows has no passwd fallback, so a tool that asks
# for one (pip, perl's File::HomeDir) fails outright without it.
USERPROFILE
# The two halves of the home directory a domain profile may use instead.
HOMEDRIVE
HOMEPATH
# Per-user and machine-wide state directories for host-tool caches.
LOCALAPPDATA
APPDATA
ProgramData
# Where 64-bit and 32-bit programs are installed. vswhere lives under the
# 32-bit tree, and CMake's own modules read these to find host tools.
ProgramFiles
ProgramFiles(x86)
CommonProgramFiles
# Default parallelism for a build tool that asks the host how wide it is.
NUMBER_OF_PROCESSORS
PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE
